EXPLAIN adalah peta rencana, bukan stopw: EXPLAIN is a plan map, not a stopwatch
`EXPLAIN` meminta PostgreSQL memilih ren: `EXPLAIN` asks PostgreSQL to choose a plan without running the statement. The result is a tree: the top node produces the final result, while lower nodes supply rows to their parent. `cost=startup..total` values are internal units the planner uses to compare alternatives in the context of configuration, statistics, and query shape. Cost is not duration and must not be read as milliseconds; a plan with total cost 100 is not automatically twice as fast as a plan with cost 200. `EXPLAIN` also does not prove that estimated rows will equal the rows that actually come out when the query runs.
Untuk membaca pohon, mulai dari kebutuha: To read a tree, start with the query's needs: which filter is selective, which relations must be joined, and whether the output must be ordered. Then read from root to child to understand the data contract, or from leaf to root to follow how rows are produced. `rows` in a plan is an estimate per loop, not an observed count. `width` is also an estimated row size. If a node looks cheap, the next question is whether its input estimate is plausible and whether the node repeats work through a parent such as a nested loop.
`Seq Scan` membaca tabel secara beruruta: `Seq Scan` reads a table sequentially. It is often sensible for a predicate that takes a large portion of a table, for a small table, or when reading the index and then the heap would cost more. `Index Scan` can find a subset through an index and is usually attractive when the predicate is selective, but heap random access and the cost of maintaining the index remain relevant. The index name does not prove that all data pages will be skipped. `Sort` adds work to order rows; input size, memory, and possible spilling affect the choice, so a small sort is not the same as a large sort.
`Hash Join` membangun hash dari salah sa: `Hash Join` builds a hash from one input and matches keys from the other input; it fits an equality join when the hash size and memory support it. `Nested Loop` runs the inner side for every outer row; this can be efficient when the outer side is small and the inner side has a suitable lookup, but becomes expensive when the outer estimate grows. `Hash Join` is not automatically better than `Nested Loop`, and `Index Scan` is not automatically better than `Seq Scan`. The planner chooses a combination of operators, not one universal winner.
Bandingkan plan dengan bukti yang memang: Compare plans using the evidence that is actually available

ANALYZE mengubah pertanyaan menjadi peng: ANALYZE changes the question into an execution measurement
`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` menjalankan statement: `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` runs the statement and then displays the plan used together with runtime information. For a `SELECT`, its data effect is usually read-only, but it still consumes CPU and locks, uses cache, and may trigger side effects from called functions. For `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, or `DELETE`, the statement can truly change data; profiling must use a safe transaction with rollback where appropriate, a disposable fixture, and suitable permission. Adding `ANALYZE` is not merely displaying more detail: it changes the operation from prediction to execution.
`actual rows` menunjukkan baris yang dih: `actual rows` shows rows produced per loop. `loops` shows how many times the node ran; on the inner side of a Nested Loop, one actual row with twenty loops can mean twenty rows in total. `actual time=start..end` is the runtime timing reported by the node, usually in milliseconds in PostgreSQL output; `start` is the time to the first row and `end` is the completion time per loop, not a wall-clock timestamp that can be compared across nodes. Parent time is inclusive: it includes child work, so adding every node's time can count the same work more than once. Compare estimated rows with actual rows to find estimate errors, but do not treat one run as a stable benchmark.
BUFFERS membantu melihat jalur buffer, b: BUFFERS helps show buffer paths, not a direct disk sensor
`EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` menambahkan: `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` adds buffer counters such as `shared hit` and `shared read`. A hit means the page was found in shared buffers at that time; a read means the page was loaded into shared buffers. These counters help show whether a query touches many pages and which nodes contribute, but `shared read` is not a promise that every page was read from physical disk. OS cache, storage, backend settings, temporary buffers, and other buffer types affect the I/O story. Conversely, shared hit is not proof that CPU work is free: checking many cached pages still requires work.
Timing, actual rows, loops, dan buffer c: Timing, actual rows, loops, and buffer counters must be read together. An inner Index Scan that is cheap per loop can become expensive when loops are large. A parent Nested Loop can report inclusive time covering all lookups. Buffer counts on nodes and parents must also be understood as plan accounting, not added without knowing whether the counter is per-node or cumulative. A good profile records the query, parameters, data state, version, configuration, cold or warm cache, and several runs before making a p50 or p95 claim. A p50/p95 baseline requires repeated queries with documented parameters and conditions, recording total duration for every run, sorting the sample, and selecting the median and 95th percentile using an agreed method. One EXPLAIN ANALYZE output or an authored number in this lesson cannot produce p50/p95.

Do not turn one run's output into an SLA; warm cache, concurrency, parameters, autovacuum, and resource contention can change the result. If a mutation must be analyzed, transaction rollback is not a solution for external side effects or non-transactional functions. This lesson teaches how to read evidence, not permission to profile production.

Planner membuat prediksi dari statistik,: The planner predicts from statistics; it does not read the whole future
Planner perlu memperkirakan berapa banya: The planner must estimate how many rows pass a predicate and how many pairs a join produces. It uses column and relation statistics such as row counts, distinct values, most-common values, histograms, and other available information. In skewed data, the frequency of one value can differ greatly from a uniform assumption. If `customer_segment = 'VIP'` actually selects most rows but stale statistics describe it as rare, the planner can underestimate the outer relation. Conversely, treating a rare value as common can make the planner choose a path out of proportion to the query result.
Estimate bukan hanya angka kosmetik. Car: An estimate is not merely cosmetic. Cardinality that is too small can make Nested Loop look cheap because the inner lookup is expected to repeat only a few times. Larger cardinality can make Hash Join or Seq Scan look more suitable. However, plan shape is a decision based on the information available during planning; it is not a promise of results, and even an accurate estimate does not guarantee the fastest query because memory, cache, parameters, parallelism, and resource contention still matter.
ANALYZE memperbarui statistik; bukan pen: ANALYZE updates statistics; it is not a replacement for EXPLAIN ANALYZE
`ANALYZE` membaca sample atau data yang: `ANALYZE` reads a sample or relevant data and updates planner statistics in the catalog. It helps the next planner see a newer distribution, but it does not run the customer-orders query to report actual rows or latency. Sampling and statistics targets mean the summary does not always contain every value. After a bulk load, a major distribution change, or an operation that makes statistics stale, ANALYZE can be necessary maintenance. For strongly correlated patterns or important distributions, suitable extended statistics or targets may be needed; that is a follow-up decision, not an automatic guarantee.
`EXPLAIN` menggunakan statistik saat men: `EXPLAIN` uses statistics to build a plan without running the statement. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` executes the statement and compares the plan with actual rows and timing. Because they answer different questions, running EXPLAIN ANALYZE is not the same as updating planner statistics, and running ANALYZE is not the same as measuring latency. For a mutation, EXPLAIN ANALYZE can change data; even a SELECT with volatile functions or external access may not be free of side effects.
Gunakan error ratio untuk memutuskan inv: Use the error ratio to guide investigation, not to blame one operator

Do not immediately force an index or change the join method because of one output. Save the query and parameters, compare estimates with actual rows, inspect statistics, and then measure the change in a representative environment.
